The voting technology company Smartmatic has pledged to bring Fox News to trial or otherwise get an apology and “full retraction” in its $2.7 billion defamation lawsuit against the right-wing channel.
This follows Fox’s $787 million settlement with Dominion Voting Systems for similar lies stemming from the network’s coverage of Donald Trump’s 2020 presidential election defeat.

As alleged by the lawsuit, Dobbs, Bartiromo, Pirro, Giuliani, Powell, and others on Fox pushed a number of false claims about Smartmatic, including that the company helped to “steal” the election from then-President Trump, that the company sent votes to foreign countries to be tabulated, and that it is a foreign company or has ties to Venezuelan dictators.

Despite clear evidence to the contrary, Fox personalities also claimed that Smartmatic and Dominion Voting Systems had related corporate ownership or other intertwined business interests and that Smartmatic was widely used throughout the country, when in fact it was used in only one county that year.
In yet another Fox mix-up between the companies, Dobbs falsely suggested that both Smartmatic and Dominion were rejected from use in Texas(it was just Dominion).
Smartmatic was used only in one county during the 2020 presidential election: Los Angeles County.
LA County leans heavily Democratic, with President Joe Biden winning 71% of the vote in 2020 and Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton winning 72% of the vote in 2016.
Giuliani and Powell baselessly and falsely claimed that Smartmatic was widely used throughout the country during the 2020 election and that its use was one of the reasons why Trump lost.
In the days and weeks following the 2020 election, Fox personalities invoked Smartmatic — along with other voting technology companies — to baselessly claim that the election was stolen from Trump.
Time and time again, the “Big Lie,” has been debunked: There was no widespread voter fraud and the election was not “stolen” from Trump.
Not only was the 2020 election the “most secure [election] in American history,” but even Trump’s own campaign research firm concluded that Trump’s claims of election fraud were incorrect.
And state and federal courts dismissed more than 50 lawsuits brought by Trump and his allies challenging the election.
Fox guests and hosts pushed a baseless and fabricated narrative that Smartmatic sent votes cast during the 2020 election to foreign countries, such as Spain and Germany, to be tabulated.
As noted in Smartmatic's lawsuit against Fox, votes were not sent abroad: Votes cast in Los Angeles County were tabulated in Los Angeles County.
Multiple Fox hosts and guests repeatedly pushed a frequently debunked claim that Smartmatic has an improper current relationship with the Venezuelan government or other foreign dictators.

Conservative media personalities drew this baseless connection to peddle the claim that Smartmatic’s technology is compromised and used to “fix elections.” In reality, Smartmatic does not have an improper current relationship with the Venezuelan government nor with other foreign governments.
Smartmatic’s founders are from Venezuela and the company’s technology has been used in Venezuela, but the company is incorporated in Florida.
And Smartmatic has not been afraid to be vocal about election interference,previously accusing the Venezuelan government of meddling in the 2017 election there.
Fox repeatedly pushed lies about Smartmatic and Dominion Voting Systems, baselessly claiming that Dominion owned Smartmatic through a Spanish company, Indra Sistemas.
Some also claimed that Dominion is a Canadian company.
Both narratives are false.
Smartmatic, Dominion, and Indra are not related and have no connection to each other.
In fact, Smartmatic and Dominion are “fierce competitor[s].” And Dominion is not Canadian; it is owned by a New York private equity firm.
